newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on improved cash demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on improved cash demand.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher on Friday, boosted by improved cash demand, traders said.
Traders noted the July contract fell as low as $11.25 per cwt, a level that attracted commercial buying interest.
"We're going to bring some business in at $11.25 (per cwt)," a trader said.

The trader added that $11.25 was also a key technical level and marked a possible breakout back to higher levels. Rice had traded above $12 per cwt in February but fell on weak cash demand and speculative long liquidation, he said.

In export news, the trade awaited confirmation of Costa Rica's rice purchase. Exporters said they likely purchased Argentine rice because it was priced lower than U.S. supplies. Tender results should be known by Monday, they said.
Rice closed 17 to two cents per bushel higher with May up 13 at $11.48.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 500 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 910 lots.
